To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we are able to generate profiles of twitter users using a variety of techniques that are able to capture the real-time nature of the web; (2) we are able, using these profiles and a collaborative filtering technique, to recommend users as followees with an accuracy that is comparable with that of existing techniques, and (3) the profiles we have developed are able to capture real-time information, and are able to adapt to changes in a user's behaviour.
we have shown that it is possible to recommend Twitter users to follow using both content- and collaborative-based techniques.

(i) the content of a user's tweets is a useful signal for predicting who might be a good followee, but (ii) collaborative information is more important, and (iii) a hybrid approach that combines the two is best.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of followee recommendation for Twitter, which is one of the largest and most popular real-time, social web services.
the problem of recommending Twitter users to follow based on their past activity.
the problem of recommending users that a Twitter user may wish to follow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best results are obtained by using a combination of content and collaborative filtering.
the content and collaborative filtering approach is the best way of recommending users to follow.
our proposed approach is able to achieve better recommendation results than the baseline methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the effectiveness of our proposed followee recommendation system, and the effectiveness of our real-time profile update mechanism.
we are able to produce recommendations with a high level of precision, with the best performing strategy having an average precision of 0.5.
content based approaches are more effective than collaborative filtering approaches, but collaborative filtering can be made to work if the data is pre-processed in a particular way.

real-time content can be used to improve recommendation performance.

real-time data can be used effectively in recommender systems, and that this can be used as a basis for a number of different types of recommendation.
